title: Your First Weekend at University of Kansas, Shared as Cards
description: A calm, under-21-safe first-weekend route through KU landmarks, public exhibits, and student-centered spaces.

cards.title: Start with the Jayhawk Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop · 1266 Oread Avenue
cards.notes: Begin by using the interactive exhibits to connect campus history and programs to the places you will encounter on the hill.
cards.short_summary: Get a visual introduction to KU before setting out across Mount Oread.
cards.evidence_claim: KU identifies the Jayhawk Welcome Center at 1266 Oread Ave. and says it has interactive exhibits about KU history and programs.
cards.access_notes: Campus-visit availability varies; the admissions page directs visitors to check current visit options.

cards.title: Pause at the Memorial Campanile
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark · 1450 Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Walk up to the memorial room and take a moment with the World War II names before continuing along Memorial Drive.
cards.short_summary: A 120-foot limestone memorial with a 53-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Campanile was dedicated in 1951; its memorial room lists 277 KU community members who died in World War II, and its carillon has 53 bells.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; carillon concerts are performed by university and guest artists.

cards.title: Follow Memorial Drive’s curve
cards.subtitle: Scenic walk · above Marvin Grove and Potter Lake
cards.notes: Use this W-shaped drive as your walking link between the Campanile, memorials, and the north-campus landscape below.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped ridge-route designed around KU’s World War II memorial.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Drive was designed to complement the Memorial Campanile and follows the crest of Mount Oread above Marvin Grove and Potter Lake.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route on the Lawrence campus; follow posted campus conditions and accessibility routes.

cards.title: Take the long way past Potter Lake
cards.subtitle: North-campus landscape · Mount Oread
cards.notes: Circle the lake on foot, then keep the stop to the banks and paths; plan a study break rather than any water activity.
cards.short_summary: A two-acre campus lake originally built as a fire-water reservoir.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Potter Lake was constructed in 1910 as a reservoir, is now a storm-water retention pond, and prohibits swimming.
cards.access_notes: Swimming is prohibited; boating is permitted only for classes and academic research, and state fishing laws apply.

cards.title: Step into the Spencer Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Gallery visit · 1301 Mississippi Street
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or current exhibition to explore slowly, then use the museum’s visitor guidance to plan the rest of your visit.
cards.short_summary: A free KU art museum with public galleries and validated garage parking.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spencer Museum of Art states that admission is free for all visitors and lists regular gallery hours, including weekend afternoon hours.
cards.access_notes: Regular hours: Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday until 8 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closures are listed by the museum.

cards.title: Meet the Panorama at the Natural History Museum
cards.subtitle: Dyche Hall · 1345 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Make the four-floor exhibit visit your main indoor stop, beginning with the Panorama and then following the displays that interest you.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history museum in Dyche Hall with the Panorama, fossils, and live-animal exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says the Natural History Museum has four floors of public exhibits, including the historic Panorama, fossils, live snakes, and insects.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed Mondays. Admission is a suggested contribution, while KU students are free.

cards.title: Regroup at the Kansas Union
cards.subtitle: Community stop · 1301 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Use the building as a practical reset: look for current programming, find a shared table, or browse its historical displays across the levels.
cards.short_summary: KU’s historic community center for events, dining, student programming, and displays.
cards.evidence_claim: KU describes the Kansas Union as a campus destination and says Student Union Activities plans more than 200 events each year for the Jayhawk community.
cards.access_notes: The Union lists building hours separately and notes that hours and access can change, including during renovations or breaks.

cards.title: Choose a seat at Watson Library
cards.subtitle: Study stop · 1425 Jayhawk Boulevard
cards.notes: Find either a group or quiet area, then try a small task such as reserving a study room or asking a librarian one question.
cards.short_summary: KU’s oldest and largest library, with quiet and group study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Watson Library, built in 1924, is its oldest and largest library and offers group and quiet study areas, workstations, scanners, and printers.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms support academic study and research; check the library’s current hours and room-reservation availability before going.

cards.title: See basketball’s original rules at DeBruce
cards.subtitle: History stop · 1647 Naismith Drive
cards.notes: Look for the original Rules of Basket Ball and the Naismith statue outside, then use the adjoining student-center spaces as a breather.
cards.short_summary: A KU student center adjoining Allen Fieldhouse and housing Naismith’s original rules.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says the DeBruce Center houses James Naismith’s original Rules of Basket Ball and includes student-center amenities and meeting rooms.
cards.access_notes: The building is connected to Allen Fieldhouse; the Union publishes current operating hours and notes game-related closures.

cards.title: Finish with a low-pressure Rec orientation
cards.subtitle: Active reset · 1740 Watkins Center Drive
cards.notes: Bring your KUID, check in at the Welcome Center, and take a first lap through the track, courts, and equipment areas at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A KU recreation facility with fitness equipment, courts, a track, climbing wall, and table games.
cards.evidence_claim: KU says Ambler SRFC has cardiovascular and resistance equipment, courts, studios, a walking/jogging track, climbing wall, table tennis, and Teqball.
cards.access_notes: Controlled-access facility for authorized KU community users; eligible participants must present valid KU or ASRFC photo ID at entry.
